headline: This law lets the U.S. Fire Administration send investigators to examine major fires and some unusual fires, then publish findings.
what_it_does: The U.S. Fire Administration can now conduct on-site fire safety investigations of major fires. Its investigators, such as safety specialists and fire protection engineers, can look at the cause of a fire and also review broader safety problems. The agency must work with federal, state, local, tribal, and territorial officials and must publish a public report, unless doing so would harm a criminal investigation. The agency can also investigate fires with unusual circumstances that cause less damage than a major fire.

who_it_affects.group: Fire departments and local fire officials
who_it_affects.how: They may have federal investigators visit the site of major fires and coordinate with them on the investigation.

who_it_affects.group: Residents and property owners in areas affected by major fires
who_it_affects.how: Federal investigators may examine what went wrong and the findings may be made public in a report.

who_it_affects.group: Fire safety researchers, codes and standards experts, and fire training specialists
who_it_affects.how: They may take part in federal fire investigations and help shape the findings and lessons learned.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 20, 2022; the summary does not state a separate effective date.
